title: What a steady tick costs

data.source: Barato and Seifert (2015); Gingrich, Horowitz, Perunov and England (2016); Gingrich and Horowitz (2017); Gabor (1946). Simulated overdamped ring and first passages, seeded.

prediction: The wider notes say one condition, C times Omega = 1, meets three uncertainty bounds at once and that cuts have a fixed spread of 0.159. The check expects three different constants (1, 0.25 and 2) and a spread that moves with the heat spent per cut, reaching 0.159 only at 78.96 kT per cut.
baseline: The thermodynamic uncertainty relation (Barato and Seifert 2015) and its first-passage form (Gingrich and Horowitz 2017).
why: In ordinary units the three bounds are met at three different numbers, about 1, 0.25 and 2, so "C times Omega = 1" is not one condition; the owner's own tier file for M21 already records the factor of 2 as structural. The spread of the gaps between cuts obeyed CV squared times heat per cut = 2: it was 0.159 only when the rotor spent 78.96 kT per cut and doubled when the spend was quartered. R1 to R6 in Phoenix make no statement about this at all; the uncertainty relation supplies one that CRR lacks.
